cannot pass turns CI red and teaches the next person to delete the gate.
Measured 2026-08-29 across all 23 URLs below (npx lighthouse, mobile preset, local preview
with the SSR document compressed the way production serves it):
total-byte-weight       max 2,834,247 (/blueprint). /project/mileway was 9,621,514 before
the gallery gifs became mp4; it is now 1,059,802.
resource-summary:script max 1,295,994 (/blueprint).
cumulative-layout-shift max 0.162 (/ops). Every other URL is at or under 0.058.
/ops re-measured 2026-09-01 after the summary layer got its height reservations and the loop
trace replaced the wrapped stat row: cumulative-layout-shift 0.0086 (npx lighthouse, mobile
preset, against `vite preview` on the production build). The other 22 URLs were NOT re-run,
so the 2026-08-29 figures above still stand for them and the fleet-wide max is now whatever

Those three are error: they are properties of the bytes and the layout, so they measure the
same on a GitHub runner as they do on a laptop. Each has roughly 20% headroom.
performance, LCP, FCP and TBT stay warn on purpose. Every number for them here came off a
developer laptop (benchmarkIndex ~4000) and this gate runs on a 2-core GitHub runner, where
they will be materially worse: /blueprint measured TBT 290 locally against the 300 budget,
so an error there would be red on the first CI run. Promote them after one calibration run
on the runner itself, not before.
cumulative-layout-shift could come down to 0.1 now that /ops has stopped shifting, but only after
all 23 URLs are re-run — tightening an error gate on one re-measured URL is how a gate that
nobody can pass gets born.
numberOfRuns is 1, not 3: this list went from 12 URLs to 23, and 23 single runs is fewer
Lighthouse runs than the 36 it was doing before. accessibility and seo, the two gates that
have always been errors, are deterministic and gain nothing from a median of three.

switcher) now defer their hydration to `@tanstack/react-start`'s `<Hydrate when={visible()}>`

/              performance 63 -> 66, LCP 6.44s -> 5.56s, TBT 19ms -> 29ms, CLS 0 -> 0.010.

That is short of the brief's aspirational 80/2.5s/300ms bar, so performance, LCP and CLS for

than being promoted to an error this site cannot pass — the whole point of the note at the top
of this file. total-blocking-time for `/` IS promoted to error below: 19-48ms measured against
a 300ms budget is a 6x-15x margin, the same 'roughly 20% headroom' bar the three existing
error assertions use, not a number picked to look good on arrival.
